week_thesis: U.S.-Iran peace deal signed June 14-15 (ceremony June 19 in Switzerland) is the dominant macro event: Strait of Hormuz reopens, oil crashes to $80 (-$4.64, -5.5%), Nasdaq surges +2.17%, SPY +0.54%. This geo-political resolution destroys the oil/energy thesis (EOG close) and rotates capital decisively into AI/tech infrastructure. Portfolio streamlines to max 3 high-conviction positions. AMAT ($591 pre-mkt, +44% from entry) and LLY ($1,137, +14.6%) are proven winners with intact theses. NVDA adds as a STRONG_BUY: $205.19 today — only +0.16% when Nasdaq is +2.17% — textbook relative-underperformance entry; 38 analysts Strong Buy; $300 avg target (+46% upside); AI infrastructure secular leader; no earnings this week. AMD skipped: $511 already 5% ABOVE consensus $486 — no margin of safety. MU: earnings June 24 = blackout. Market closed Friday June 19 (Juneteenth).

buys.reasoning: Relative underperformance today (+0.16% vs Nasdaq +2.17%) in a broad tech rally = textbook accumulation entry. 38 analysts Strong Buy consensus as of June 14; avg 12-month target ~$299-300 (+46% upside from $205.19). New SharonAI 6-year AI compute partnership announced. CEO Jensen Huang forecasts $200B CPU TAM; Vera CPUs for China launching August (new revenue stream, bypasses export restrictions). Nvidia dominates 85-92% of AI accelerator market with no credible near-term challenger. Blackwell architecture ramp intact. No earnings risk this week. Iran peace deal removes geopolitical uncertainty that had been weighing on global AI capex decisions — expect acceleration of data center buildout worldwide. RSI ~50 (neutral, no overbought risk). Previous June 8 trade plan targeted NVDA at $205 — same price, second opportunity to enter as execution was missed. Best risk/reward in the universe at this level.

close_reasoning.EOG: U.S.-Iran peace deal destroys the oil thesis entirely. Strait of Hormuz reopens immediately — oil drops to $80 (-$4.64, -5.5% today). EOG had been flagged for closure in multiple prior plans (RSI 70.4 overbought in bars; oil headwind; planned close in May/June). Iran deal is the definitive catalyst: energy geopolitical premium collapses, oil likely tests $75-78 range as Iranian production resumes. Entry $138.58; last known +2.65% (+$748). Close to lock remaining gain and eliminate sector risk.

Last known +10.75% (+$150) on 23 shares. Tiny position with negligible capital impact; semi equipment thesis fully covered by AMAT (+44%). Simplify portfolio to reach 3-position max.

hold_reasoning.AMAT: Portfolio's strongest performer at ~+44% from $411.45 entry (current ~$591, pre-market +4.25% to $591.38). AI semiconductor equipment multi-year super-cycle: SCREEN Semiconductor Solutions joined EPIC Center partnership (May 2026), semi equipment growth outlook >30% for 2026. Iran peace deal is constructive: global trade normalization improves supply chain and expands semiconductor addressable markets worldwide. Analyst avg target $511 has been exceeded — but AMAT continues to benefit from secular AI capex tailwind. RSI ~67 (approaching overbought; monitor). Hold with trailing stop ~$508 (5% below $534 mid-Jun range). Do not add — let winner run.
hold_reasoning.LLY: Eli Lilly ($1,137 current, +14.6% from $992.17 entry) remains a defensive healthcare anchor. Retatrutide Phase 3 TRIUMPH-1 cleared (28.3% weight loss — class-best). Mounjaro Q1 revenue +125% YoY. FY2026 EPS guidance $35.50-37.00. 31 analysts Buy consensus; $1,211 avg 12m target (+6.5% further upside). Healthcare is defensive in elevated-rate environments; low correlation to geopolitical events. RSI ~70.3 (nearing overbought) — monitor; do not add. Hold with stop ~$942.

skip_reasoning.AMD: Strong fundamental story (Q1 DC revenue $5.8B +57% YoY; BofA target $560; Venice CPU launch catalyst) but $511.57 current price is 5% ABOVE the $486.33 consensus analyst target. Chasing a name above consensus with 130% YTD gain carries meaningful mean-reversion risk. Today's +4.73% surge on Iran deal rally adds to chase concern. Revisit if AMD pulls back to $470-480 range.
